name: Invisible Collar
description: Invisible Collar is a high rubber-guard clinch in which the bottom player keeps an arm isolated and closes the second leg high behind the opponent's head to reinforce posture control.
variant_uniqueness: High two-leg clinch with an isolated arm
summary: Invisible Collar is a high rubber-guard clinch in which the bottom player keeps an arm isolated and closes the second leg high behind the opponent's head to reinforce posture control.
overview:
The bottom player faces the kneeling or leaning top player in a high guard. One arm has been isolated through the New York and neck-clearing sequence. The second leg closes high behind the head to reinforce the first controlling leg. The bottom player maintains the knee hug and uses the hips to keep the enclosure comfortable.

The collar is a leg-based posture-control configuration; it does not require a jacket collar or place the attacker behind the opponent. Neck-cleared arm isolation distinguishes the basic path from a high guard that still contains both arms. Terminology: Invisible Collar control.

Keep the elbow separated from an inside frame before closing the second leg. Maintain the cleared hand position and knee hug as the free leg comes higher. Bring the second leg into the high clinch through hip motion; do not pull the foot into position against resistance.

Avoid sustained neck compression, forced stacking, and foot pulling against a fixed knee. Agree on verbal taps and open both the hand and leg controls immediately on a stop signal.

Instructional sources: [Eddie Bravo — MTS 134 Invisible Collar in Austin](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KCyIwacRKu8); [Eddie Bravo — Chill Dog / Invisible Collar clarification](https://www.10thplanetjj.com/forum/threads/17657-Chill-Dog-Invisible-Collar-Question).
key_principles: Retain the isolated arm: Keep the elbow separated from an inside frame before closing the second leg.
Preserve neck clearance: Maintain the cleared hand position and knee hug as the free leg comes higher.
Close without knee torque: Bring the second leg into the high clinch through hip motion; do not pull the foot into position against resistance.
Use connected leg pressure: Hold the upper body close with the whole leg configuration rather than squeezing or wrenching the neck.
Read the free arm: Monitor frames and posture so an arm extraction does not silently undo the control.
Open to recover guard: Release the high clinch and rebuild ordinary frames if the position becomes a stack or causes knee discomfort.

top.name: Invisible Collar Top
top.description: Invisible Collar top perspective: The free leg moving behind your head is an attempt to reinforce posture control, even without a collar grip. Keep the head aligned and the captured elbow compact rather than twisting against the enclosure.
top.overview:
The top player is responsible for recognizing and defending the control. The bottom player faces the kneeling or leaning top player in a high guard. One arm has been isolated through the New York and neck-clearing sequence. The second leg closes high behind the head to reinforce the first controlling leg. The bottom player maintains the knee hug and uses the hips to keep the enclosure comfortable.

The free leg moving behind your head is an attempt to reinforce posture control, even without a collar grip. Keep the head aligned and the captured elbow compact rather than twisting against the enclosure. Avoid driving all weight onto the partner's shoulders while the legs are locked high.

Create space at the hip and thigh before trying to raise the head or extract the arm. Bring the elbow back between the bodies after the high closure opens. Tap immediately to a choke or joint pressure; posture recovery is an early defense, not a late escape guarantee.

The collar is a leg-based posture-control configuration; it does not require a jacket collar or place the attacker behind the opponent. Neck-cleared arm isolation distinguishes the basic path from a high guard that still contains both arms. Avoid sustained neck compression, forced stacking, and foot pulling against a fixed knee. Agree on verbal taps and open both the hand and leg controls immediately on a stop signal.

The high leg-and-arm enclosure can create vascular choke pressure when it closes around the sides of the neck. Misplaced pressure against the windpipe or a sideways pull that becomes a neck crank is a reason to open the enclosure, not squeeze harder. Do not mistake the absence of a jacket grip for the absence of a choke: tap before neck compression develops, and wait for both legs and the controlling arm to release before lifting posture.

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar defense: what is the free leg trying to achieve as it moves behind your head?
flashcards.answer: The free leg moving behind your head is an attempt to reinforce posture control, even without a collar grip.

plausible: Form a triangle regardless of elbows
Put the shin beneath the chin
trap: Replace high leg with a waist clamp

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar defense: how should you manage your head and captured elbow while still enclosed?
flashcards.answer: Keep the head aligned and the captured elbow compact rather than twisting against the enclosure.

plausible: Twist head and extend trapped arm
Pull elbow wide to lift your chin
trap: Rotate torso with the neck fixed

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar defense: where does forward stacking weight concentrate on the guard player?
flashcards.answer: Driving forward under the high legs can fold the bottom player onto the shoulders and neck. Keep a balanced base and create space instead of using that compression to force a release.
flashcards.answer_line: Across the shoulders and upper back

plausible: Across hips, upper back unloaded
Into bent knees, shoulders raised
trap: Through hands, with the torso free

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar defense: how should you create room before recovering upright posture?
flashcards.answer: Create space at the hip and thigh before raising the head or extracting the arm. Pulling against a fixed knee or trapped shoulder does not safely supply that clearance.
flashcards.answer_line: Frame hip and thigh, then raise head

plausible: Pull ankle sideways, knee fixed
Lift chin with high legs closed
trap: Drag wrist, leaving shoulder fixed

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar defense: after the high closure opens, where should the isolated elbow return?
flashcards.answer: Bring the elbow back between the bodies after the high closure opens.

plausible: Far outside their raised knee
Straight past the opposing head
trap: Behind your torso, hand on mat

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar defense: why is early posture recovery different from a late escape guarantee?
flashcards.answer: Tap immediately to a choke or joint pressure; posture recovery is an early defense, not a late escape guarantee.
flashcards.answer_line: Neck or joint may already be loaded

plausible: A higher chin means shoulder freed

trap: No neck risk once knee hug loosens

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar defense: what new contact must you account for after the free leg rises?
flashcards.answer: The opponent faces you from high guard. The second leg reinforces the posture-control enclosure, so the original high shin is no longer its only leg contact.
flashcards.answer_line: A second leg bracing the first

plausible: A low ankle crossing replaces shin
Both hands on collar, high legs open
trap: Your elbow inside the first knee

bottom.name: Invisible Collar Bottom
bottom.description: Invisible Collar bottom perspective: Keep the elbow separated from an inside frame before closing the second leg. Maintain the cleared hand position and knee hug as the free leg comes higher.
bottom.overview:
The bottom player is responsible for maintaining the control. The bottom player faces the kneeling or leaning top player in a high guard. One arm has been isolated through the New York and neck-clearing sequence. The second leg closes high behind the head to reinforce the first controlling leg. The bottom player maintains the knee hug and uses the hips to keep the enclosure comfortable.

Keep the elbow separated from an inside frame before closing the second leg. Maintain the cleared hand position and knee hug as the free leg comes higher. Bring the second leg into the high clinch through hip motion; do not pull the foot into position against resistance.

Hold the upper body close with the whole leg configuration rather than squeezing or wrenching the neck. Monitor frames and posture so an arm extraction does not silently undo the control. Release the high clinch and rebuild ordinary frames if the position becomes a stack or causes knee discomfort.

The collar is a leg-based posture-control configuration; it does not require a jacket collar or place the attacker behind the opponent. Keep knee fixed while turning foot
trap: Hold until they lift you upright

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar control: which body adjustment helps the reinforcing leg reach comfortably?

Let knee drift with the foot caught
trap: Turn away, bent leg fixed under load
